business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law at the federal and criminal law level; Civil Law of Quebec origin for Quebec private law; federal statutes and provincial regulations coexist)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between Canada, the United States of America, and the United Mexican States (USMCA/CUSMA)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Convention between Canada and the United States of America with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital, signed September 26, 1980, as amended
Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (FIPAs) applicable to Canadian investors as ratified by Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and its regulations, including the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, as amended; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1; Quebec Charter of French Language, CQLR c C-11; FINTRAC interpretative guidance and policy directives; and applicable sanctions legislation, including the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c 21.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for any non-Quebec corporate general partner or corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or equivalent competent authority in the entity's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the limited partnership agreement and declaration or registration instrument
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or governmental registry of the document's origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, register of partners, or register of individuals with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or applicable corporate registry in the foreign jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Quebec attorney for service and local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the state of issue is not a party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity, address, and beneficial ownership verification package for each individual with significant control, including passport copies, proof of residential address, and structural ownership charts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office, financial institution, notary, or licensed professional in the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy and Hague Apostille; consular legalization if the certifying state is not an Apostille state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against OFAC SDN List, Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, and domestic politically exposed person (PEP) databases. Enhanced due diligence applies to foreign PEPs, individuals identified in adverse media, and jurisdictions with strategic AML deficiencies. FINTRAC reporting obligations include suspicious transaction reports, large virtual currency transaction reports, and terrorist property reports where applicable. Reliance on nominees or shell entities is prohibited unless the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner is fully identified and verified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Registre des entreprises (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name of a limited partnership formed or registered in Quebec must be in French. A name in another language may be used only if the French version is presented sufficiently in the corporate name or additional French-language elements are included. Latin-character transliteration is required for names originating in non-Latin scripts. The name must not contain obscene words, may not be likely to mislead, and must comply with Quebec's Charter of the French Language and the naming guidelines of the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire des entreprises du Québec refuses the proposed name, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration within 30 days of the refusal, accompanied by the original decision and available supporting facts. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, an administrative appeal may be made to the Administrative Division of the Court of Québec within 30 days of the notice. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately reserve a revised name through the online portal and pay the applicable new reservation fee. For names rejected due to similarity with an existing registered name, a written consent obtained from the prior registrant may be submitted as grounds for reconsideration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for the Quebec registered office and service of process address, provided it consists of a valid, physical street address in Quebec and is not a post-office box. For an online cosmetics retail limited partnership, virtual office arrangements are accepted by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, but the entity must maintain sufficient director, records, and agent substance in Quebec. If the virtual office is the only physical presence, heightened scrutiny may arise in bank account opening, sales tax registration, and interprovincial registration processes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the stated low-risk online retail business: approximately 15% annual probability of a compliance-oriented records examination, including potential outreach rather than physical presence. The likelihood rises to approximately 40% if the registry receives complaints, there are missing or late filings, cash is accepted, or adverse media is identified. Unannounced physical inspections are rare in the absence of specific regulatory red flags or court-ordered enforcement activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236 et seq. (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 21-31.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Quebec Enterprise Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or escrow account requirement. Each limited partner must contribute the capital specified in the limited partnership agreement (C.C.Q. art. 2262); general partners may contribute value as agreed and any deficiency is corrected under the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first meeting of the general partner of the limited partnership, that: (1) the proposed limited partnership agreement, including capital contribution requirements and allocation of profits and losses, is approved and adopted; (2) the registered office of the limited partnership shall be fixed at [address], Quebec, and the declarants are authorized to file all statutory records; (3) [General Partner Inc.] is appointed as general partner and [Manager Name] is appointed as manager, with authority to bind the partnership exclusively in the ordinary course; and (4) the manager is authorized to file the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, open bank accounts and payment-rail accounts, and execute all ancillary agreements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Name Authorization from the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name authorization portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name request through the REQ 'Services en ligne' portal, providing at least three proposed names. Include the mandatory legal designator 'L.P.' or 'société en commandite / S.E.C.' The registrar will issue a certificate of name authorization valid for 90 days, during which the registration declaration must be filed.
required_dossiers: Completed name request form
Proof of identity of the general partner
Letter of authorization if an agent files on behalf of the partnership
Supporting memorandum on name distinctiveness if the name includes recognized words
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name request is refused, review the REQ refusal reasons and resubmit within 30 days with a revised name, or file an administrative response before the REQ to cure deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary in Quebec (recommended) or external legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and fully execute a written limited partnership agreement under C.C.Q. arts. 2236-2244. The agreement must state the capital contributions and withdrawal conditions of limited partners, management powers of the general partner, profit-sharing ratios, admission mechanisms, and restrictions preventing limited partners from participating in management. Maintain the original signed counterpart for inspection by the REQ and financial institutions.
required_dossiers: Executed limited partnership agreement
Proof of identity and residential address of each general partner
Capital contribution record or bank proof
Certificate of name authorization issued by REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agreement is defective or incomplete, obtain a unanimous written consent of all partners and amend the agreement by a supplementary deed before filing the registration declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration of Registration with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ online system and submit the Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite. The declaration must include the legal name, principal establishment address in Quebec, the names and residential addresses of all general partners, and an express statement that it is a limited partnership. Attach the name authorization certificate and pay the statutory fee. The REQ then issues an enterprise number (NEQ) and the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Name authorization certificate
Duly signed declaration of registration
Copy of the limited partnership agreement if requested by REQ
Authorization of the general partner appointing the filing person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of deficiency, file an amendment under s. 31 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises within 30 days, attach the missing schedules, and pay any applicable processing fee to prevent deregistration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Provincial Tax and Occupational Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec; Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST); municipal licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued NEQ, register the limited partnership with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and any applicable employer deductions. If the partnership is an employer, create a CNESST workplace health and safety account. For the physical premises, submit a municipal commercial occupany permit application or a simple business license where required by municipal by-law.
required_dossiers: REQ certificate of registration (NEQ)
General partner identification
Bank account details of the limited partnership
Lease or proof of commercial occupancy for the registered premises
Business plan if required by the municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec or CNESST requests additional information, respond through the secure message center within 15 days; if registration is refused, supply updated documentation and re-apply, or request a formal administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Establish Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or credit union selected by the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the REQ certificate of registration and executed limited partnership agreement to the commercial banking department. Open a Canadian business account in the limited partnership's name, appoint signatories in accordance with the partnership agreement, and connect Shopify Payments and PayPal merchant accounts to the partnership bank account.
required_dossiers: REQ certificate of registration (NEQ)
Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement
Resolution appointing authorized signatories
Identification documents of all officers and managers
Proof of Canadian registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the application due to enhanced due diligence, provide CRA/Revenu Québec registrations and a certified copy of the declaration of registration; if refusal persists, resubmit to another Canadian financial institution or request a compliance review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None — ISIC 4791 online retail of cosmetics is not an industrial activity in Quebec and no provincial industrial operating license is prescribed; physical premises remain subject to municipal zoning and fire-safety by-laws.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial industrial operating license required; an optional municipal commercial occupancy permit (certificat d'occupation) may be required by local by-law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category C retail occupancy; no mandatory environmental impact assessment under the Québec Environmental Quality Act (Schedule EIA is not triggered by non-industrial warehousing).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No specific industrial discharge thresholds apply; wastewater must comply with municipal sewer by-laws, volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions are negligible from packaged cosmetics, and waste handling must meet the Règlement sur l'enfouissement et l'incinération des matières résiduelles where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A fire safety inspection certificate from the competent municipal fire prevention service is required for any commercial premises; workplace safety registration with CNESST is required upon first hiring; the premises must comply with the Québec Building Code provisions for means of egress, fire alarms, and structural safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — My Business Account portal and Business Registration Online; for Quebec-specific taxes (QST, provincial income tax deductions), Revenu Québec / Services Québec online portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign limited partnership carrying on business in Canada/Quebec must apply for a Business Number (BN) from the CRA using Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC348. The BN serves as the GST/HST registration number for the partnership itself; in Quebec, separate registration for QST is effected through Revenu Québec, generally using the same BN and a distinct TVQ account. Non-resident suppliers are required to register once their taxable supplies in Canada exceed C$30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the aggregate over the preceding four consecutive quarters. For the Quebec QST, the equivalent threshold applies. The LP is a separate 'person' for GST/QST purposes but is not a taxpayer for income tax purposes; each partner must report its allocable share on its own Canadian tax return, and non-resident partners may need a CRA tax account for instalment remittances.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a check-the-box regime. A limited partnership is characterized by law and remains fiscally transparent for Income Tax Act purposes. No entity-level classification election is available for a Canadian LP. For cross-border hybrid mismatch scenarios, the Income Tax Act hybrid entity rules (ss. 18.1 and 18.2) apply de jure to disallow double deductions or deduction-without-inclusion outcomes, and no advance election is needed for these anti-avoidance provisions to operate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) — Canadian VAT-type indirect tax system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000: GST/HST registration is mandatory for any person (including non-resident suppliers and online sellers) making taxable supplies in Canada above this threshold in either a single calendar quarter or the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. Quebec imposes a parallel C$30,000 threshold for QST registration. For non-resident e-commerce operators, a simplified GST/HST and QST registration regime applies to taxable supply categories such as remote goods supply and digital services where Canadian-source sales exceed C$30,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal invoice clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping mandate. Registered suppliers must issue invoices containing prescribed GST/HST/QST information; however, those invoices are not pre-validated by the CRA or Revenu Québec. Electronic filing of GST/HST and QST returns is mandatory for large registrants and available to all registrants through CRA's GST/HST NETFILE/API and Revenu Québec's E-services, but no government fiscal invoice approval API is involved.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: exports of tangible personal property supplied to a non-resident and shipped by or on behalf of the supplier from Canada to an outside-Canada destination are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, of the Excise Tax Act, provided prescribed documentary evidence is retained and the goods leave Canada within statutory timelines. Services: supplies of services to a non-resident are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7, if the services are not in connection with Canadian real property or tangible personal property located in Canada and are not reasonably expected to be received by a person in Canada. For Quebec QST, analogous zero-rating provisions apply. In a beauty DTC e-commerce context, each export sale must be supported by ordered goods, shipping documentation, and proof that risk and possession passed outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration (Form B13A or CAED / G7 export report)
Bill of lading, airway waybill, or Canada Post/courier waybill for low-value shipments
Proof of export (carrier attestation, customs export permit, eManifest receipt, or port stamp)
Bank transfer/remittance record or payment processing statement evidencing receipt of foreign consideration and FX repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rated export claims within the normal reassessment period of four years, extended to seven years for misrepresentation, neglect, or wilful default. If export substantiation is inadequate or fraudulent, the supply is recharacterized as a domestic taxable sale, exposing the LP to assessment of 5% GST and 9.5% QST (14.975% combined) plus interest, failure-to-file penalties, and, for gross negligence, a penalty equal to 50% of the understated tax. Criminal prosecution for willful tax evasion or false statements may result in fines up to C$10,000 on summary conviction or up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment, in addition to full reassessments and retrospective zero-rating clawbacks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange control administration. Financial supervision is exercised by OSFI for banks and by FINTRAC for currency-flow reporting and money-services-business compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely floating, and no prior exchange approval is required for profit remittance, loan repayments, intercompany settlement, or capital distributions to non-residents. For a Quebec limited partnership, the sole legally relevant hurdles are tax reporting and withholding consequences, not currency regulation: non-resident partners allocated Canadian-source business income may be taxable under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Quebec Taxation Act, with treaty relief available under an applicable tax treaty. Contemporaneous transfer pricing, partnership allocation schedules, and substance documentation are required to avoid reassessment under anti-avoidance rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no minimum holding-period requirement for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or converted into CAD through a Canadian Authorized Foreign Exchange Dealer. Reporting obligations are limited to Canada Border Services Agency export declarations for goods, FINTRAC large-cross-border-transaction reports on monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more, and routine income tax and provincial sales tax compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for non-bank fintech EMI payment facilitation, but low suitability as the primary or sole CAD clearing account. A foreign EMI not licensed as a bank under the Bank Act (Canada) has no direct membership in Payments Canada and cannot clear or settle CAD-denominated transactions on its own. An overseas EMI may operate in Canada only through a FINTRAC-registered money-services-business, with settlement ultimately occurring through a Canadian chartered bank. Such EMIs are acceptable as a secondary disbursement rail, provided the main treasury liquidity account remains at a tier-1 Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate onboarding is generally possible using FINTRAC-compliant digital identity verification and notarized corporate packages, but a Quebec LP with non-resident beneficial owners is generally subjected to enhanced due diligence. The authorized signatory and general partner will typically need a live video interview, and in practice most tier-1 banks require at least one principal to attend an in-person appointment at a Canadian corporate banking centre for onboarding or for approval of a non-resident ownership structure. Remote opening may proceed immediately only where the entity has a substantial Canadian nexus, verified beneficial ownership, and a clean source-of-wealth package.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque limited-partnership ownership or nominee partners concealing ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organization chart covering every LP unit holder; registered partnership records; powers of attorney; trust declarations or foundation constitutional documents; certificates of incumbency for corporate partners; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation; executed legal opinion from qualified Canadian counsel identifying all ultimate beneficial owners and confirming no nominee ambiguity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident general partner or non-resident principals without demonstrable Canadian substance or business nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec establishment and business number registrations; GST/HST and QST registration; office or warehouse lease; payroll and operational substance records; website and fulfilment service-level documentation; Shopify store registration; jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction corporate ownership synopsis; board or partnership resolution authorizing the Quebec banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated consumer payment flows received through Shopify Payments and PayPal creating an unclear source-of-funds trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling Shopify settlement reports and PayPal activity statements; chargeback and refund breakdowns; product purchase records and invoices; reconciliation against general ledger; third-party payment processor agreements; monthly revenue forecasts and payment-rail transaction logs; sales tax remittance summaries demonstrating alignment of reported revenue with banked receipts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident partners should be routed as SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers using the local bank's account name, address, and bank identifier code. Canada and Quebec do not impose a domestic FX purpose code, but the originating jurisdiction may require a purpose code: for such jurisdictions, use the category denoting direct investment or capital contribution, and add the remittance narrative 'Capital contribution to a Canadian limited partnership.' The receiving bank will perform beneficiary scrutiny, sanctions screening, and source-of-funds checks; supporting documentation should be delivered in advance, including the executed partnership subscription agreement, capital call notice, shareholder or partner resolution, source-of-wealth evidence, and the LP's bank-account opening package. Intra-Canada settlement for large-value CAD payments takes place over Lynx, while lower-value payments may be cleared through the Automated Clearing Settlement System.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for procurement of cosmetics inventory and fulfilment services should be made by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer for open-account transactions, or by an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued through SWIFT MT700 when the supplier requires LC terms. Domestic CAD disbursements clear through Payments Canada ACSS; cross-border USD disbursements require the Canadian bank's US correspondent network. Payments intended for China, the European Union, or other destinations can be executed in CAD or foreign currency after conversion at the authorized dealing rate. Each payment must be supported by the purchase invoice, bill of lading or waybill, certificate of origin where applicable, and any relevant permit; all parties, banks, and intermediaries must be screened against Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, as well as against OFAC lists where the US dollar is involved.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/EUR or CAD/CNY deliverable forward contracts approved by the Canadian counterparty desk
Currency options on CAD pairs for hedging committed procurement exposure
Cross-currency swaps pairing CAD with the functional currency of the partner jurisdiction, limited to cash-flow hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only for non-convertible or restricted trade currencies such as onshore CNY, with documented commercial hedge rationale

Forwards, swaps, and options entered into exclusively with OSFI-regulated Canadian Schedule I banks or their approved foreign-currency subsidiaries; speculative derivative positions are prohibited under the partnership treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual enterprise declaration (declaration annuelle) - Quebec public-register re-registration statement; serves as the equivalent of a franchise tax return (no franchise tax in Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire d'entreprises du Quebec (REQ), Ministere de la Justice (Quebec enterprise register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the 60 days following the close of the LP fiscal period (for a December 31 fiscal period: due on or before March 1 of the next year; for a materially different fiscal period, due 60 days after that period closes); the declaration reconfirms the legal address of the establishment, the general partner(s), the activity code NAICS 456120 and the LP's registered agent information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: REQ sends a notice of default; if the declaration remains unfiled 60 days after the notice, the enterprise registration is administratively struck off. During a lapse of publicity, limited partners lose the statutory limited-liability shield against third parties, and offences carry fines of CAD 400-4,000 (legal person) or CAD 200-1,000 per involved individual; directors/general partners may also face separate personal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return, T5013 Summary and T5013 slips (allocation of income/loss to partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return and Summary due no later than the last day of the fifth month after the partnership fiscal period (May 31 for a December 31 year-end); each partner must receive the T5013 slip by March 31 of the year following the fiscal period; the CRA copy of the slip accompanies the Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100) up to CAD 2,500 for a partnership with 100 or fewer partners; CAD 25/day up to CAD 7,500 for larger partnerships; partners who rely on late allocations may be reassessed with arrears interest and penalty under ITA section 163

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Releve 15 (RL-15) partnership information slip - Quebec partner allocation report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with Revenu Quebec and delivered to each Quebec-resident partner no later than the last day of March following the reference fiscal period (calendar-year basis); electronic transmission is accepted and must meet the same statutory date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted RL-15 attracts a CAD 25 per day penalty (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per slip); misreported allocations may be reassessed with interest and, in cases of gross negligence, penalties up to CAD 4,000 under the Tax Administration Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual return (TPS) for Canadian e-commerce registrant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If on an annual filing basis with a December 31 fiscal period, the return and any balance due are due on or before March 31 of the next year; GST/HST registration is mandatory once taxable worldwide revenue from Canadian supplies exceeds CAD 30,000 over any four consecutive calendar quarters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file: penalty equal to 5% of the unremitted balance plus 1% per complete month of default (maximum 12 months); a repeat failure within three years triggers 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; interest is compounded daily on unpaid amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec sales tax (TVQ/QST) annual return for online cosmetics retailer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Revenu Quebec, Direction generale des taxes (QST file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an annual QST registrant with a December 31 fiscal period, the TVQ annual return and remittance are due on or before March 31 following the year; mandatory QST registration in Quebec applies to a business with taxable supplies arising in Quebec above CAD 30,000 per calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Revenu Quebec imposes a 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months) on the unpaid balance; for a second failure within three years: 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months, with daily compound interest applied pursuant to sections 91, 94 and 96 of the Tax Administration Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises or the Civil Code of Quebec solely because of size or revenue. An audit becomes compulsory when triggered by: (i) the limited partnership agreement or unanimous-partner covenants, (ii) a lender, investor or franchisor requiring audited statements, (iii) the LP being a reporting issuer or otherwise publicly accountable, or (iv) an order of a court or regulator. Market practice: an annual audit is prudently introduced when gross revenue exceeds CAD 1,000,000, when third-party debt is obtained, or when a corporate general partner's governance rules require it
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) is the default framework for a private Quebec LP; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; income allocation to partners is computed under the adjusted partnership income rules of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Quebec Taxation Act, using the same accounting framework consistently

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not issue a separate annual UBO return for limited partnerships. The annual declaration filed with REQ must be kept current, and any change in general partners, limited partners whose identity is recorded, or a corporate general partner's ultimate beneficial owners must be filed as a REQ amendment within 30 days of the event. At each annual declaration, the LP must verify the register file, confirm the recorded partner identities, refresh the ultimate-beneficiary particulars of any corporate partner, and document the confirmation in the minute book. Transfer or pledge of a partnership interest is ineffective against the LP and third parties until the REQ amendment is recorded
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180-440 per year (CAD 250-600) for a Quebec registered-office or formation-agent service, where the general partner does not maintain a physical establishment; low end covers agent mail-forwarding and address listing, high end covers compliance notice handling and REQ amendment preparation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,200-5,500 per year (CAD 3,000-7,500) for a full audit/assurance engagement of a Shopify-based beauty e-commerce LP, including ASPE conversion, partner-allocation review and tax-basis reporting; a review engagement will typically fall below this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal (15%) and Quebec (11.5%) general corporate income tax rate; a Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and pays no entity-level tax — income is allocated to partners and taxed at the partner level (the 26.5% rate applies to a corporate general partner resident in Quebec).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD): a Canadian-controlled private corporate partner may claim the combined federal (9%) and Quebec (3.2%) reduced rates on the first CAD 500,000 of eligible active business income, producing an effective combined rate of 12.2%; Quebec also offers a 10-year tax holiday for qualifying new manufacturing businesses in designated regions, though not relevant to a pure online beauty retail business, and scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) credits for eligible digital and product-development expenditures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 — Partnership Information Return (federal, CRA) and TP-600 — Quebec Partnership Information Return (Revenu Québec), E-filed through approved Canadian tax software portals (CRA My Business / Revenu Québec CLIC).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013 must be filed no later than the last day of the sixth month after the partnership fiscal period end; TP-600 must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end if all partners are Canadian resident individuals, otherwise within six months.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross business revenue from online sales of cosmetics, personal care products, shipping income, and ancillary commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue attributable to Canadian-source business carried on through the Quebec permanent establishment; expenses and income must be allocated to each partner jurisdiction-consistently.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit computed as gross revenue less cost of goods sold (product costs, freight-in, packaging, direct online payment fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must use the same arm's-length cost base; treaty rules on permanent establishment must be considered before claiming Canada may not tax the allocated business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net partnership business income or loss, allocable among general and limited partners in accordance with the limited partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the non-resident partner's allocable share on the partner's own Canadian Part I return (T1 or T2) if Canada has taxing jurisdiction under the applicable tax treaty; the partnership must not withhold Part XIII tax on this business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of limited partners and their allocations, including residency, share of income, contributions, and any admitted limited liability protection.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify each non-resident limited partner by full legal name, country of tax residence, and tax identification number; attach a statement of the basis for treaty relief if the partner claims no PE is created.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty for T5013 is CAD 25 per day, per partner, up to CAD 2,500 per partner; TP-600 late filing carries a penalty of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500, plus additional administrative penalties under Quebec tax legislation for willful non-filing, including a fine of up to CAD 25,000 and, in aggravated cases, imprisonment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 — Corporation Income Tax Return (federal, CRA) and CO-17 — Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (Revenu Québec), E-filed via CRA and CLIC portals; required for any corporate partner receiving an allocation of income from the Limited Partnership.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Corporate taxation year applies — both T2 and CO-17 are due six months after the corporate partner's fiscal year-end; taxation year of the corporate partner does not necessarily coincide with the LP fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Active business income: includes the partner's allocated share of the LP's Canadian-source business income from online cosmetics retail and related services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner reports the allocated share as taxable Canadian business income only if the partnership's Quebec establishment constitutes a permanent establishment of the non-resident partner under the applicable treaty; otherwise the income is exempt under Part I treaty rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec/Federal dividend deductions and intercompany adjustments; used to reconcile allocations and to claim the Small Business Deduction on Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) active business income eligible for the reduced rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned corporation cannot claim the CCPC SBD; the general corporate rate (26.5% combined) applies to its allocated share without the federal-provincial small business rate reduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable after applying federal and Quebec tax abatements, credits, and refundable portions of investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners compute tax under Part I and must attach a T2 Schedule 13 (foreign tax credit) or equivalent Quebec schedule to avoid double taxation of the same allocated business income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (max 12 months) for federal and Quebec; failure to file electronically or to provide required schedules attracts additional penalties; knowingly filing false corporate returns can trigger fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Canadian Income Tax Act, applied to dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; distributions by a Limited Partnership to a non-resident limited partner are not legally dividends and are not subject to Part XIII withholding — they are taxed as allocable Canadian business income on the non-resident partner's own return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower treaty withholding rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the Canadian payer with a completed Form NR301 — Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty (or NR302 for a flow-through partnership), together with a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction, and, upon request, additional economic-substance documentation; the payer must make a reasonable determination that treaty benefits apply. If excessive tax was withheld, the non-resident may request a refund from the CRA on Form NR7-R, generally within two years after the end of the calendar year of withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate for royalties (including trademark, brand, and technology licensing) and interest paid to non-residents is 25%; under most Canadian tax treaties the rate is reduced to 10% for non-arm's-length royalties and 10% or 0% for arm's-length interest; certain copyright- and know-how-related royalties paid to U.S. residents are exempt under the Canada-U.S. treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: T106 — Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions is mandatory when the aggregate fair market value of cross-border transactions with related non-resident persons exceeds CAD 250,000 in a taxation year; comprehensive OECD-compliant Local File and Master File documentation is expected under CRA administrative policy when aggregate related-party transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000 and the consolidated group revenue exceeds CAD 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act, and Quebec's parallel anti-avoidance provisions, permit reassessment and denial of tax advantages where transactions lack genuine economic substance and are carried out primarily to avoid tax. Additionally, Quebec civil law provides that a limited partner who takes part in the management or control of the Limited Partnership loses limited liability and is jointly and severally liable for partnership debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting online sales revenue from the Shopify or PayPal payment rails, overstating cost of goods sold through inflated related-party invoices, or submitting false information to the CRA or Revenu Québec on T5013, T2, or TP-600 filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 239(1): fine of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment for up to five years; Quebec Tax Administration Act: additional civil penalties of up to CAD 100,000 plus prosecution costs and compound interest on unreported liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers of the corporate general partner face criminal prosecution and are personally liable for the corporation's unremitted source deductions and GST/QST under section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act; civil asset seizure, travel bans, and restrictions on leaving Canada may be imposed through Revenu Québec enforcement measures, and fraudulent conveyance of partnership assets can pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Quebec Limited Partnership as a passive invoicing vehicle to divert e-commerce profits to a foreign low-tax related entity while all substantive retail functions — purchasing, storage, online marketing, and customer service — remain in Canada, producing no real economic activity in the partnership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of interposed entity treatment under the GAAR; reassessment of profits to the Canadian beneficial owner; accuracy-related penalties of up to 25% of the misstated amount under section 163(2); Quebec administrative penalties of up to CAD 50,000 for false statements or omissions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Limited partners found to have exercised control or management authority are stripped of limited liability under the Quebec Civil Code and become jointly and severally liable for all partnership obligations; directors of a foreign corporate general partner may be held personally liable for Canadian taxes arising from a sham structure, with extended civil restitution and, in criminal cases, extradition exposure where a tax treaty permits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and T106 Omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length prices for cross-border procurement of cosmetics, brand royalties, or online marketing services without contemporaneous documentation; failing to file T106 for related-party transactions exceeding CAD 250,000; maintaining a deliberately thin margin for the Canadian partnership while foreign affiliates retain residual profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under section 247(2) to the arm's-length price; penalty under section 247(3) equal to 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment where documentation is absent or inadequate; interest and arrears running from the original assessment date; Quebec may apply an equivalent reassessment and penalty regime aligned with the federal adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorize underpricing or who grossly negligently fail to obtain proper documentation may be named in a transfer pricing penalty assessment; if the partnership or corporate partner defaults, directors can be liable for unremitted withholdings, and director residency restrictions may be ordered by the CRA where a taxpayer's principal residence is outside Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-volume e-commerce payments through Shopify Payments and PayPal without implementing risk-based AML procedures, transaction record retention, or suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC; accepting large cash-equivalent or digital-currency payments from non-resident sources without beneficial-ownership verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act of up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for failure to maintain a compliance program, report suspicious transactions, or keep required records; criminal penalties are also available, including fines and imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of a corporate general partner may be subject to personal penalties where they failed to implement reasonable compliance measures, including personal fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment; the CRA and Revenu Québec may also levy civil penalties against directors who knowingly fail to report taxable revenues underlying the payment flows.
